                <h1 class="entry-title">Maharashtra: Sugarcane farmers continue highway blockade at Kini for second day; insist on Rs 4,500 first instalment</h1>

                

                <div class="td-module-meta-info">
                    <div class="td-post-author-name"><div class="td-author-by">By</div> <a href="https://www.chinimandi.com/author/vivek-waghmode/">Vivek Waghmode</a><div class="td-author-line"> - </div> </div>                    <span class="td-post-date"><time class="entry-date updated td-module-date" datetime="2026-11-04T12:36:35+05:30">November 4, 2026</time></span>                                                        </div>

            </header>


        </div>

        

        <div class="td-post-content tagdiv-type">
            <div class="td-featured-image-rec">

            <div class="td-post-featured-image"><a href="https://www.chinimandi.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Protest-01.jpeg" data-caption="" class="td-modal-image"><img width="364" height="205" class="entry-thumb td-animation-stack-type0-2" src="https://www.chinimandi.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Protest-01.jpeg" srcset="https://www.chinimandi.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Protest-01.jpeg 364w, https://www.chinimandi.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Protest-01-300x169.jpeg 300w, https://www.chinimandi.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Protest-01-150x84.jpeg 150w" sizes="(max-width: 364px) 100vw, 364px" alt="" title="Protest 01"></a></div>            </div>

            <p>Kolhapur: The indefinite highway blockade launched by the Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana at Kini Toll Plaza, demanding a first instalment of Rs 4,500 per tonne for sugarcane, continued for a second day on Wednesday, with no breakthrough reported even after 24 hours of protest. Traffic on the Pune-Bengaluru National Highway remained severely disrupted as farmers refused to vacate the protest site.</p>
<p>The agitation began on Tuesday afternoon under the leadership of former MP Raju Shetti, with hundreds of sugarcane growers from surrounding areas joining the protest. Farmers spent the night on the highway and continued their agitation on Wednesday. Arrangements were made at the protest site to provide tea, breakfast and other food to the participants.</p><div class="td-a-rec td-a-rec-id-content_inline  tdi_43 td_block_template_1">
<style>.tdi_43.td-a-rec{text-align:center}.tdi_43.td-a-rec:not(.td-a-rec-no-translate){transform:translateZ(0)}.tdi_43 .td-element-style{z-index:-1}.tdi_43.td-a-rec-img{text-align:left}.tdi_43.td-a-rec-img img{margin:0 auto 0 0}.tdi_43 .td_spot_img_all img,.tdi_43 .td_spot_img_tl img,.tdi_43 .td_spot_img_tp img,.tdi_43 .td_spot_img_mob img{border-style:none}@media (max-width:767px){.tdi_43.td-a-rec-img{text-align:center}}</style><a class="whatsapp_middle_ad" href="https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029Va4oJRZDJ6GsFXMA2x1o" target="_blank"><img alt="ChiniMandi WhatsApp Channel" src="https://www.chinimandi.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ChiniMandi-WhatsApp-Channel-banner.webp" class="td-animation-stack-type0-2"></a></div>
<p><strong>Farmers refuse to withdraw agitation</strong></p>
<p>The protesting farmers have maintained that they will not call off the agitation under any circumstances until their demand for a first instalment of Rs 4,500 per tonne is accepted. They have decided to continue the highway blockade until a settlement is reached.</p>
<p>Highway police have arranged traffic diversions at several locations between Karad and Kagal and appealed to commuters to use alternative routes. The diversions have been put in place at Karad and Peth Naka towards Pune, and at Sangli Phata, Toap, Wathar, Kagal and Uchgaon Phata towards Kolhapur.</p>
<p>Meanwhile, according to sources Kolhapur District Collector Vijay Rathod was likely to intervene to resolve the deadlock. He is learnt to have sought a proposal from sugar mills.</p>
<p>The proposed payment structure is yet to result in a resolution, while farmers continue to insist on their demand for Rs 4,500 per tonne as the first instalment.</p>

farmers</span><div></div></div></section></div> </div></div>KOLHAPUR: For the commuters travelling along Pune-Bengaluru National Highway, take note that along the stretch at Kini Toll Naka, the blockade by sugarcane farmers over their demand of higher cane price continues on Wednesday morning as well.<span class="id-r-component br" data-pos="2"></span>Around 20 hours into the blockade led by ex-MP Raju Shetti started, no govt minister or it's representative have approached the protesters to end the blockade.<span class="id-r-component br" data-pos="4"></span>Hundreds of cane farmers slept on road overnight including Shetti who night earlier has warned to stop the milk and vegetables supply to Mumbai and Pune if the price demand is not met.<span class="id-r-component br" data-pos="6"></span>According to the highway police, the traffic diversions have been placed at various locations along the stretch from Karad to Kagal and they have appealed commuters to follow diversions strictly to avoid further inconvenience. <!-- -->The trucks continues to remain stranded across both sides of the protest venue.<span class="id-r-component br" data-pos="12"></span>The diversions are at Karad, Peth Naka towards Pune side, at Sangli Phata, Toap, Wathar, Kagal, Uchgaon Phata towards Kolhapur side of the highway.<span class="id-r-component br" data-pos="14"></span>According to ths sources, Kolhapur district collector Vijay Rathod is likely to step in. He is learnt to have sought proposal from the millers that they are willing to pay between Rs 3,800 to Rs 3,900 per ton as first installment and Rs 150 to Rs 200 per ton after crushing season.<div                 <h1 class="entry-title">Raju Shetti mobilises sugarcane farmers for November 3 highway blockade over Rs 4,500 first instalment demand</h1>

                

                <div class="td-module-meta-info">
                    <div class="td-post-author-name"><div class="td-author-by">By</div> <a href="https://www.chinimandi.com/author/vivek-waghmode/">Vivek Waghmode</a><div class="td-author-line"> - </div> </div>                    <span class="td-post-date"><time class="entry-date updated td-module-date" datetime="2026-11-02T11:58:16+05:30">November 2, 2026</time></span>                                                        </div>

            </header>


        </div>

        

        <div class="td-post-content tagdiv-type">
            <div class="td-featured-image-rec">

            <div class="td-post-featured-image"><a href="https://www.chinimandi.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/raju-shetty-farmer-leader.webp" data-caption="" class="td-modal-image"><img width="500" height="500" class="entry-thumb td-animation-stack-type0-2" src="https://www.chinimandi.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/raju-shetty-farmer-leader.webp" srcset="https://www.chinimandi.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/raju-shetty-farmer-leader.webp 500w, https://www.chinimandi.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/raju-shetty-farmer-leader-300x300.webp 300w, https://www.chinimandi.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/raju-shetty-farmer-leader-150x150.webp 150w, https://www.chinimandi.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/raju-shetty-farmer-leader-420x420.webp 420w" sizes="(max-width: 500px) 100vw, 500px" alt="raju shetty farmer leader" title="raju shetty farmer leader"></a></div>            </div>

            <p>Kolhapur: Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana founder and former MP Raju Shetti has announced an indefinite road blockade at the Kini toll plaza on the Pune-Bengaluru National Highway from November 3, demanding a first instalment of Rs 4,500 per tonne for sugarcane supplied by farmers.</p>
<p>The agitation, scheduled to begin at 11 am, is being organised to press for the pending demands of sugarcane growers and protest against what the organisation describes as the failure of sugar mills and the government to ensure remunerative prices for their produce. Thousands of farmers are expected to participate in the protest.</p><div class="td-a-rec td-a-rec-id-content_inline  tdi_43 td_block_template_1">
<style>.tdi_43.td-a-rec{text-align:center}.tdi_43.td-a-rec:not(.td-a-rec-no-translate){transform:translateZ(0)}.tdi_43 .td-element-style{z-index:-1}.tdi_43.td-a-rec-img{text-align:left}.tdi_43.td-a-rec-img img{margin:0 auto 0 0}.tdi_43 .td_spot_img_all img,.tdi_43 .td_spot_img_tl img,.tdi_43 .td_spot_img_tp img,.tdi_43 .td_spot_img_mob img{border-style:none}@media (max-width:767px){.tdi_43.td-a-rec-img{text-align:center}}</style><a class="whatsapp_middle_ad" href="https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029Va4oJRZDJ6GsFXMA2x1o" target="_blank"><img alt="ChiniMandi WhatsApp Channel" src="https://www.chinimandi.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ChiniMandi-WhatsApp-Channel-banner.webp" class="td-animation-stack-type0-2"></a></div>
<p>As part of the mobilisation campaign, Shetti is touring Sangli district on November 2 to rally support for the agitation. He has also been conducting an extensive tour of villages in Kolhapur district’s Shirol and Hatkanangale talukas, holding meetings and corner gatherings to mobilise sugarcane growers.</p>
<p>During his tour, Shetti visited Dattawad, Abdul Lat, Akiwat, Shirti, Bubnal, Nandani, Udgav, Kothali, Danoli, Narande, Alte and Rui. Farmers turned out in large numbers at these meetings and expressed their support for the proposed agitation.</p>
<p>Questioning the refusal of sugar mills to increase cane prices, Shetti said sugar prices in the open market had increased, while prices of by-products such as bagasse and molasses had also risen significantly.</p>
<p>Shetti warned that the November 3 agitation would not be a one-day protest but an indefinite movement, describing it as a decisive struggle for the rights and livelihood of sugarcane farmers.</p>
<p>He appealed to farmers from Shirol and Hatkanangale talukas, as well as other areas, to participate in large numbers and assemble at the Kini toll plaza to press for the demand of a Rs 4,500 per tonne first instalment.</p>

Pune-Bengaluru highway over prices</span><div></div></div></section></div> </div></div>KOLHAPUR: The 120-km stretch of the Pune-Bengaluru National Highway (NH-48) between Nagthane near Satara and Sangli Phata near Kolhapur remained deserted on Wednesday as sugar cane farmers continued their blockade for a second day, demanding a higher cane price.<span class="id-r-component br" data-pos="2"></span>Chief minister <a href="https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/topic/devendra-fadnavis" styleobj="[object Object]" class="" commonstate="[object Object]" frmappuse="1">Devendra Fadnavis</a> said, “Govt fixes the fair and remunerative price, which the mills pay. The issue of price is between millers and farmers. We have asked minister Hasan Mushrif to initiate talks and resolve the situation.”<span class="id-r-component br" data-pos="6"></span>Led by the Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana, the blockade began at 10am on Wednesday at Nagthane in Satara district and the Kini toll booth in Kolhapur district. Hundreds of trucks remain stranded on both sides of the highway.<span class="id-r-component br" data-pos="11"></span>Police have diverted traffic travelling between Mumbai-Pune and Kolhapur-Bengaluru via Rahimatpur, Pusesavali, Sangli, Ankali and Sangli Phata. “We left Mysore with a consignment of cooking oil to be delivered in Mumbai. But we have been stuck on the highway since Tuesday afternoon. We have no food to eat, no drinking water,” a truck driver said.<span class="id-r-component br" data-pos="13"></span>The sudden diversion of traffic led to severe congestion in towns and villages along the alternate route. <div data-type="in_view" class="  "><div class="js_tbl_2ad"></div><div class="mgid_second_mrec_parent"><div id="taboola-mid-article-thumbnails-135548661" class="" data-target_type="mix" data-mode="thumbnails-mid" data-placement="Mid Article Thumbnails 1" data-pagetype="article" style="max-height:415px;overflow:hidden" data-ua-type="2" onclick="stpPgtn(event)"></div></div></div>Police said patrolling teams were helping stranded truckers with food and water.<span class="id-r-component br" data-pos="17"></span>Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana leader Raju Shetti is demanding Rs 4,500 per tonne for sugar cane. “Farmers are willing to settle for Rs 4,200 per tonne,” he, however, said on Wednesday evening, adding, “Mushrif proposed Rs 3,850 per tonne, which we have rejected.”<span class="id-r-component br" data-pos="20"></span>Announcing that the agitation would continue at least till Thursday, Shetti said: “The travellers are facing troubles because govt, which is the guardian of all of us, is ignoring the demand. <!-- -->We have decided to observe a bandh in Kolhapur, Sangli and Satara districts if govt does not accept the price demand. Our demand is not irrational. The millers are selling sugar at Rs 5,400 per quintal and they want us to get only FRP, while keeping the rest of the money for their elections.<!-- -->”<span class="id-r-component br" data-pos="25"></span>Meanwhile, Centre-appointed expert Ramesh Chand held discussions with stakeholders from the sugar industry.
